summary: Skamania County, WA 20-foot wooden tower built in the 1930s and now gone; footings and phone-line insulators remain on an abandoned road a one-mile walk from Forest Road 8851.

facts.design: 20-foot wooden L-5 tower with a cab; Willhite reads it as a 20-foot pole tower with added stairs and numerous pole supports
facts.status_note: Gone per firelookout.com and its index; Willhite does not know when it was destroyed; footings remain at the site

access.note: Reached by a walk of about one mile on an abandoned road from Forest Road 8851; the sources describe no closure

visit.trail_note: No tower remains to climb. The old road ends at the top of a steep hillside above the Lewis River.

events.note: Photographs on Willhite's page are dated October 19, 1935; the build date is given only as sometime in the 1930s

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com gives a 20-foot tower (used for facts.height_m). Willhite's notes place the panoramic photos on the roof at 20 feet plus 15 feet for the cab, which suggests a taller total. The story says the total height is unclear.

sources.title: Switchback Lookout Site - Gifford Pinchot National Forest

notes_for_editor: Brief status 'gone' and tower type are supported. Public access is inferred from a national-forest road and a described one-mile walk with no closure in the sources; confirm with the Gifford Pinchot ranger district before publishing. The build date has no year in the sources, so the only dated item is the 1935 photographs (event 'other'). No staffing or fire history appears in these sources, so none is written. Willhite's 2019 visit is the only observation of the site today.
